children: Ukraine's central bank raised its key rate by half a point to 16% on Thursday, delivering a rare consecutive increase as inflationary pressures persisted amid intensified Russian air attacks on economic infrastructure, officials said.

The central bank said in a statement that the upward pressure on prices remained high due to the consequences of the war with Russia and the conflict in the Middle East, which has squeezed global energy supplies.
Ukraine's consumer inflation quickened to 8.1% year-on-year in August, from 7.7% in July, official data showed.

"Core inflation has remained high in recent months," said Central Bank Governor Andriy Pyshnyi. "The intensification of Russia's targeted attacks on industrial and infrastructure facilities is exacerbating medium-term inflationary risks."

With fighting on the front line largely stalled more than four-and-a-half years into the war, Moscow and Kyiv have targeted logistics networks and other economic assets in an effort to undermine each other's war effort.
For more than two weeks, Russia has carried out near-constant attacks on the capital Kyiv using faster jet-powered drones, disrupting life, business and government operations.

Due to the intensified Russian air attacks, the central bank may cut its forecast for gross domestic product growth to 1.1-1.2% this year, from its previous target of 1.8%, Deputy Governor Volodymyr Lepushynskyi told an online media briefing.
The rate increase was expected by analysts. A poll by ICU, a Kyiv-based investment bank, showed that more than 65% of those polled had expected a rise.
However, some expressed concern about the accessibility of bank financing for Ukrainian businesses that desperately need funds to recover and rebuild.
"The scope to curb inflation by raising interest rates is limited," said Danylo Hetmantsev, the head of the parliamentary committee on finance, tax and customs policy.
"A higher interest rate will not rebuild the devastated energy sector, nor will it bring down the price of oil or resolve transport difficulties," Hetmantsev said on Telegram.

To help Ukrainian businesses adapt and support the economy, the government has expanded the existing war risk insurance program and simplified processes for claiming compensation, Prime Minister Sergii Koretskyi said on Thursday.
